result.summary:
Ran `docker compose up -d` (via `sudo -n docker compose up -d`, this host's docker.sock requires sudo; both letflow-1-postgres-1 and letflow-1-keycloak-1 were already Up/healthy on port 5463 per this workspace's untracked .env LETFLOW_DB_PORT=5463) then `TEST_PARALLEL_N=4 scripts/test_parallel.sh` in the foreground, blocking for the full ~6m47s run, after `source ~/.asdf/asdf.sh` and `export WASMEX_BUILD=true`.

Actual combined output (verbatim from the aggregator):

  test_parallel: N=4 (source: env override)
  test_parallel: TEST_POOL_SIZE=21 (computed: N=4, max_connections=100, superuser_reserved=3, headroom=10, nonpool_reserve=2)
  partition 1: 735 tests, 2 properties, 0 failures, exit 0
  partition 2: 801 tests, 4 properties, 0 failures, exit 0
  partition 3: 737 tests, 0 properties, 3 failures, exit 2
  partition 4: 779 tests, 0 properties, 0 failures, exit 0
  ---
  combined: 3052 tests, 6 properties, 3 failures (3055/3058 passed)
  real 6m46.938s

3 failures total, all in partition 3, all pre-existing known failure classes unrelated to this branch's supervision-tree change (verified by reading partition-3.log directly, not inferred):

1. `Mix.Tasks.Letflow.CheckToolchainTest` "a matching rust pin reports OK with no mismatch" (test/mix/tasks/letflow_check_toolchain_test.exs:274) -- `** (ErlangError) Erlang error: :enoent` from `System.cmd("rustc", ["--version"])` at lib/system.ex:1141. Matches the documented rustc-ENOENT class (no rustc toolchain installed in this environment).
2. `Mix.Tasks.Letflow.CheckToolchainTest` "a mismatched rust pin reports a MISMATCH row naming expected and running" (test/mix/tasks/letflow_check_toolchain_test.exs:289) -- same `:enoent` root cause as #1.
3. `Letflow.Engine.Lua.ExecutorTest` "global isolation (AC3) a global written in execution 1 is absent in execution 2" (test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs:64) -- `right: {:error, {:wallclock_timeout, 5000}}` instead of `{:ok, _}`. Matches the documented Lua wall-clock-timeout-under-contention flake per docs/issues/ISS-0426.yaml (this test runs inside a 4-way-parallel partitioned run sharing host CPU, exactly the contention condition ISS-0426 describes).

None of the 3 failures touch `Letflow.Obs.Alerts`, `Letflow.Scheduler.Poller`, `Letflow.Application`, or any TaskSupervisor-related test -- confirmed by grepping partition-3.log for those names against the failure list, zero matches. All alerts_test.exs, poller_test.exs, and application-boot-ordering-relevant tests passed across all 4 partitions. No genuine regression attributable to this branch's `Letflow.Obs.Alerts.TaskSupervisor` addition or application.ex child-ordering change was found.

Verdict: full-suite run confirms REVIEWER's targeted 28+41-test regression sweep -- 3055/3058 passing, 3 pre-existing/environmental failures unrelated to ISS-0429, 0 new regressions.
